_comment: Events power both the map pins and the timeline scrubber. 'year' is the timeline anchor: a single integer where negative = BCE (e.g. -586 = 586 BCE). 'year_end' is set only for ranges or continuous traditions. 'precision' tells the UI how to label/treat the date: exact | circa | traditional | legendary | range | continuous. 'tradition_note' carries belief-framing and any contested-site sensitivity so the app can present claims respectfully rather than as asserted fact. 'description' is intentionally a strong starter paragraph; expand toward the 'great detail' goal in the content pipeline.

events.title: Birth of the Prophet Muhammad
events.description: Muhammad was born in Mecca around 570 CE into the Quraysh tribe. Orphaned young, he grew up to become a trader known for trustworthiness before, in Islamic belief, receiving the prophetic call.
events.tradition_note: Revered in Islam as the final prophet. The exact birth year is traditional and approximate.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Muhammad was born in Mecca around 570 CE into the Quraysh tribe. Orphaned young, he grew up to become a trader known for trustworthiness before, in Islamic belief, receiving the prophetic call.

events.title: The First Revelation
events.description: In Islamic tradition, while meditating in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nour, Muhammad received the first verses of the Qur'an through the angel Jibril (Gabriel), beginning the prophetic mission.
events.tradition_note: Described here as understood within Islamic tradition.

sections.heading: The night in the cave
sections.body: By his early forties, Muhammad had taken to withdrawing for days at a time to a cave on Jabal al-Nour, outside Mecca, for solitude and reflection. Islamic tradition holds that on one such night in the month of Ramadan, an angel appeared and commanded him to recite. Overwhelmed, he returned home shaken to his wife Khadija, who reassured and supported him. This encounter is remembered as the beginning of the Qur'anic revelation.

sections.heading: In the texts
sections.body: The opening five verses of Surah Al-'Alaq are traditionally held to be the first revealed, beginning with the command to read or recite in the name of the Lord who creates. The early verses of Surah Al-Muddaththir are also counted among the earliest. The encounter itself is preserved in the hadith literature, most fully in the narration attributed to Aisha at the start of Sahih al-Bukhari.

sections.heading: Place & moment
sections.body: Jabal al-Nour (the 'Mountain of Light') rises northeast of Mecca; the small Hira cave near its summit is today a site of visitation. Tradition places the event around 610 CE, when Muhammad was about forty.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: This night marks, in Islamic belief, the start of roughly twenty-three years of revelation that together form the Qur'an, and the beginning of Muhammad's mission as a prophet.

references.note: Traditionally held to be the first verses revealed.
Among the earliest passages in the traditional sequence.

references.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Revelation (hadith of Aisha; ~no. 3)
references.note: Hadith numbering varies by edition; verify against the connected Hadith source.

events.title: The Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj)
events.description: In Islamic tradition, Muhammad made a miraculous night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and an ascension through the heavens. The event ties Jerusalem closely to Islam, marked today by the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque.
events.tradition_note: A matter of Islamic belief. Jerusalem is sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam; present multiple traditions' perspectives.

events.title: The Hijra: Migration to Yathrib (Medina)
events.description: In 622 CE Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Yathrib, soon renamed Medina. The migration marks the start of the Islamic calendar and the formation of the first Muslim community.

events.description: In 630 CE Muhammad returned to Mecca largely peacefully, after which the Kaaba was rededicated as a center of monotheistic worship.

events.description: Muhammad died in Medina in 632 CE. His tomb lies within Al-Masjid an-Nabawi (the Prophet's Mosque), the second-holiest site in Islam.

events.description: In 680 CE Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of Muhammad, was killed at Karbala. The event is central to Shia Islam and commemorated each year during Muharram.

events.title: Birth of Jesus
events.description: Christian tradition places the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. The Church of the Nativity marks the traditional site. Most scholars date the birth to a few years before 1 CE.
events.tradition_note: Honored as a prophet in Islam as well. Birth year is debated.

sections.heading: A birth in Bethlehem
sections.body: The Christian Gospels narrate the birth of Jesus to Mary in Bethlehem. Luke describes a journey for a Roman census, a child laid in a manger, and shepherds drawn by an announcement of his birth; Matthew adds visitors from the east following a star, and the family's flight from Herod. The Church of the Nativity now stands over the traditional site.

sections.heading: Across traditions
sections.body: The birth of Jesus is revered beyond Christianity. In Islam, Surah Maryam recounts the birth of Jesus ('Isa) to Mary as a sign and a mercy, and Mary is honored as among the most exalted of women. Reading the two accounts side by side is one of the things the Sacred Map is built to make possible.

sections.heading: Place & moment
sections.body: Bethlehem lies just south of Jerusalem in what was then Roman Judea. Scholars generally date the birth to a few years before the conventional start of the Common Era.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: For Christians, the birth (the Nativity, celebrated at Christmas) marks the entry of Jesus into the world and is foundational to the faith's account of his life.

references.note: Joseph's dream and the visitors from the east.
The Islamic account of the birth of Jesus to Mary.

events.tradition_note: A foundational belief in Judaism; also honored in Christianity and Islam. The mountain's location and dating are debated.

events.description: Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469 at Rai Bhoi di Talwandi, now Nankana Sahib in Pakistan. His teachings of one God, equality, and honest living shaped the faith.

events.title: Birth of the Buddha
events.description: Siddhartha Gautama, later the Buddha, was born at Lumbini in present-day Nepal. The site is a major pilgrimage destination and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
events.tradition_note: Scholarly dates vary; some place the Buddha's life roughly a century later.

events.title: The Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya
events.description: Beneath the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, Siddhartha attained enlightenment and became the Buddha. The Mahabodhi Temple marks the site.

events.title: The First Sermon at Sarnath
events.description: At the Deer Park in Sarnath, the Buddha delivered his first teaching, setting in motion the 'wheel of dharma' and founding the early monastic community.

sections.heading: Setting the wheel in motion
sections.body: Tradition holds that after his awakening at Bodh Gaya, the Buddha travelled to the Deer Park at Isipatana, near present-day Sarnath, and taught five former companions. This first discourse is remembered as the 'turning of the wheel of Dhamma' and the beginning of the Buddhist community (Sangha).

sections.heading: In the texts
sections.body: The discourse is preserved in the Pali Canon as the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta. In it, the Buddha sets out a middle way between extremes and presents the framework of the Four Noble Truths.

sections.heading: Place & moment
sections.body: Sarnath, just north of Varanasi on the Ganges plain, became one of the four principal places of Buddhist pilgrimage and a major monastic center in later centuries.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: As the first formal teaching, the sermon is foundational: it introduces the core framework many Buddhist traditions build upon and marks the start of the community that carried the teaching across Asia.

references.note: The first discourse; the Four Noble Truths and the Middle Way.

events.title: The Buddha's Parinirvana
events.description: At Kushinagar the Buddha entered parinirvana, his final passing. The site became one of the four principal places of Buddhist pilgrimage.
